I've got to be realistic online scams run rampant across the web in the past You needed to hold on to your physical wallet, but these days you'll need to keep your passwords close and your personal details closer There are many people in organizations that may try to scam you they'll access your online bank account Fraudulently use your credit card or learn your pin to use your debit card. So be vigilant and stay aware
FINLIT 101 · Avoiding Scams: protect your information · selected excerpt, used with permission.
Which action addresses Casey’s reused-password risk?
This short practice check saves with your lesson work. You can change your answer after reading the feedback.
Follow a complete example
I read Casey's original post and the audience setting together. A time in a private draft is different from the same time in a public post. Casey's account settings make the original post public, so the place/time inference is relevant. I do not infer Casey's exact address from a community-centre sign.
Connect the video to this task. The video explains why information can matter. The example makes the response specific by pairing each visible clue or account habit with a relevant control.


Next I separate content from access. Casey's password reuse could connect the social and music accounts if that shared credential were stolen. Removing the photo does not resolve reuse. I therefore recommend content changes, permissions and account controls separately.


Complete audit:




Casey's original post combines a recurring Tuesday departure time with a recognizable community-centre sign and a public audience. A stranger may infer part of Casey's routine and use team details in a convincing payment message. The post does not prove an exact home address or a current compromise. Casey could remove the routine caption and replace the image with a neutral background, then share later with approved contacts. Casey should also restrict unneeded continuous location permission; that reduces new app access but does not remove existing image clues or copies.


The social and music accounts reuse a password. Casey should use a different strong credential for each through the independently opened services, consider a password manager, enable supported MFA on the social app and confirm the recovery route. These reduce access risk; they do not authenticate every message. A repeatable habit is to check photo backgrounds, time/location detail and audience before posting, and review permissions after app changes. This plan uses the Canadian source record checked September 28, 2026; actual settings must be checked in the actual service.




“Turning the account private guarantees nobody can share the old photo” fails because the fictional control guide explicitly preserves that limitation. “The team badge proves identity theft has happened” also goes beyond the record.

Recognize scams and verify independently

Core vocabulary
Pretending to be another person or organization to gain trust.
A deceptive attempt to obtain information or access by posing as a trusted source.
Checking through a route obtained separately from the suspicious message.
A feature that raises a concern and calls for verification; it is not by itself a complete proof.
Start here
A familiar logo, a person's name or professional writing can make a message look convincing. The more useful question is what the sender wants you to do. A request to move money, reveal a code or install software deserves a pause even when the message looks polished.


You will classify several common fraud approaches, follow a bank message and a call claiming to be from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), practise choosing an independent verification route, and then prepare a response to a new job offer and a possibly genuine bank contact. Your product will identify the request, evidence, uncertainty and safe next step. The aim is careful verification, not assuming every unexpected contact is fraudulent.


Follow Meet the situation and read the documents → Learn the method → Follow a complete example → Practise with support → Check your understanding → Apply independently → Review and complete. Pause between the examples if useful. All required documents are supplied and answers save automatically. Guided work and six questions are practice; the final response plan and sign-offs form your evidence.


Vocabulary. Phishing is a deceptive contact designed to obtain information, money or access. Impersonation means pretending to be a trusted person or organization. A warning cue is a reason for concern, not complete proof of identity. Independent verification uses a route found separately from the questionable contact. A one-time code can authorize access or a transaction; it is not a harmless reference number.


Optional reference disclosure: Official scam and CRA guidance. The local dated records are sufficient. No student must open a website, call anyone, install software or send money.


Meet the situation and read the documents


Leah is a fictional adult reviewing an inbox. Leah has not clicked, replied, transferred money or shared a code. The following training cards show the whole relevant request; there are no hidden attachments to inspect.


Document A — Two contacts for the worked example






Contact
Complete supplied wording and context





A: bank-looking text, October 6, 10:15 a.m.
“Your money is at risk. Move your balance to our protected account within ten minutes. Reply with the sign-in code we just sent. Keep this investigation private.” It displays a bank name, but sender identity is not verified. Leah has a bank card and the previously installed bank app.




B: caller claiming to be CRA, October 6, 11:00 a.m.
“I am Alex from a CRA processing office. We need to discuss a document supporting your return. I can provide my name, office location and callback number for you to verify.” No payment, password or code is requested in this supplied exchange. Leah filed a return, but has not verified this caller. Caller ID displays a government-style name.





Card B could be a genuine contact. That possibility does not authenticate it. Leah can end the call and independently verify before sharing information.


Document B — Five other requests to classify


All are fictional examples with unverified senders.






Card
Supplied request





C: investment pitch
“Guaranteed 20% return every week. Send $300 to the platform I chose today; there is no risk. Do not ask your bank because they will block your opportunity.”




D: job offer
“We did not need an interview. Pay a $75 account-upgrade deposit to unlock your first paid online tasks. The balance on our screen proves your earnings.”




E: emergency claim
“It's your cousin. My phone broke. Send $200 now to this new contact so I can get home. Please do not check with anyone else.”




F: purchase offer
“Concert tickets at a very low price. Leave the marketplace payment system and transfer immediately to reserve them. I cannot show proof that I hold the tickets.”




G: relationship message
A person Leah has only met online writes, “I care about you. Send $150 for my emergency trip to visit. If you trusted me, you would keep this between us.”





Document C — In-course source records


Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (CAFC), selected fraud descriptions and warnings; checked September 28, 2026: investment pitches may promise unrealistic guaranteed returns; job fraud may require payments to unlock work; emergency impersonation may demand urgent secret payments; merchandise fraud may use fake listings or payment claims; relationship fraud may build trust before requesting money. A scheme can combine types. The CAFC's current impersonation warning identifies “safe account” transfers and requests for codes or remote access as dangerous instructions; independently contact the actual institution.


CRA, “Verify it's the CRA calling,” checked September 28, 2026: CRA does call people. If uncertain, do not give personal information during the unverified call. Ask for the person's name, office and callback details, end the call, and use CRA's independently reached verification tool or official contact route. Caller ID is not proof. The tool does not include every direct employee number; an unrecognized result needs further official checking, not an automatic fraud verdict.


Read the documents


Which action in Card A creates the clearest immediate financial/access risk? Choose and select Check document reading.
Learn the method
Read the requested action first


A scam often tries to move a person from uncertainty to an irreversible action quickly. Identify the verb: send, transfer, install, reveal, deposit, approve. Then identify what could be lost: money, account access, personal information or control of a device. This is more reliable than judging a logo or spelling alone; convincing messages can be well written.


Pressure can be emotional as well as financial. A threat of closure, a promise of easy earnings, fear for a relative or a claim that love requires payment can all discourage checking. Recognizing the mechanism helps you pause without blaming the person receiving it. These approaches are designed to exploit ordinary hopes and responsibilities.


Classify by the story and the requested benefit


The label helps explain a pattern; it does not replace evidence. Card C offers investment returns, so investment fraud is the relevant pattern. Card D offers employment but asks the worker to pay, matching a job-fraud pattern. Card E impersonates a loved one in difficulty. Card F offers goods without adequate verification, matching a purchase/merchandise concern. Card G uses a developing relationship to seek funds.


Types can overlap. A supposed romantic partner who later recommends a guaranteed investment combines relationship and investment tactics. An online job that asks you to receive and forward money is different from ordinary paid work, even if it uses a real company's name. The CAFC advises verifying the actual employer independently and not paying deposits to unlock a job. A company existing does not prove that its name is being used by an authorized recruiter.


Break the sender's control over verification


Calling a number supplied only in the message keeps you inside the same contact's story. A separate route changes that. For a bank, use the number on a card or statement already held, or open the known bank app directly. For a family emergency, use the person's previously known number or another independently known contact. For an employer, find the real organization's official contact information independently and ask about the named vacancy and recruiter. Do not install an offered app or send money while checking.


For an investment, the source recommends independent research and registration checks with the provincial securities regulator or the national registration search. Registration is one check, not a guarantee of returns or proof that a message's sender is the registered person. This course does not ask you to evaluate or buy a real investment.


Keep the possibility of genuine contact open


CRA may need supporting tax information and may call. Therefore, “CRA never calls” is not a safe rule. Neither is “they knew my name, so I should answer everything.” The taught process lets a real request be handled through a verified route while denying an impersonator control of the interaction.


Asking for callback details collects a claim to check; it does not verify the claim. End the call before checking. Reach the CRA verification page independently. If its tool cannot verify a direct number, use the official CRA contact route for further checking. A result about a listed number also does not make caller ID impossible to spoof. The next conversation must use a route you have verified yourself.


Use a short decision record






Part
Example from Card A





Request
Transfer the balance and reveal a code.




Cues
Time pressure, secrecy, “protected account” story, access code.




What is unknown
Actual sender and whether there is a real bank issue.




Immediate boundary
No transfer, code sharing or message link use.




Independent check
Known bank app or contact details on the existing card.





The result of verification may be “request confirmed,” “fraud attempt confirmed,” or “still unresolved.” If unresolved, do not treat pressure as evidence. If exposure has already occurred, shift promptly to the response process in the next lesson rather than continuing the conversation.

In this lesson, “double-check” means reaching the organization through a separate, independently obtained route—not calling a number just because the message supplies it.

FINLIT 101 · Avoiding Scams: pause and verify · selected excerpt, used with permission.
Which action independently checks the bank-looking request?
This short practice check saves with your lesson work. You can change your answer after reading the feedback.
Watch a worked decision
Pause, verify, then act
This demonstration includes a bank-looking message and a CRA web notice. The lesson record uses a bank-looking text and a caller claiming to be CRA. Follow the independent-verification method, then respond to the exact contact channel and request in the lesson cards.
Pause and decide: For the two fictional contacts, identify the requested action, one warning cue, and the verification route.
Read the narrated and visual transcript
Slide 1: Two messages, two requests
Read the action—not just the logo. A  “Move your money to our safe account. Send the code.”; B  “A new tax notice is available.”. What does each contact want you to do?
Two fictional contacts arrive. A bank-looking text says a transfer is at risk and asks the person to move money to a “safe account” and reply with a one-time code. A second notice says a tax message is waiting and tells the person to sign in through the usual government route. A familiar logo or official-sounding name does not identify the sender. Start by underlining the action each message requests and decide whether it is reversible or sensitive.
Slide 2: Spot pressure and sensitive requests
A cue raises concern; verify before acting. Urgency or threat; Transfer to a “safe” account; One-time code or password; Remote access or unusual payment. Cue ≠ proof • pause before an irreversible action.
Scams often create urgency, secrecy, threats, or an unexpected reward. Requests to transfer money to a “safe account,” buy gift cards, use cryptocurrency, install remote-access software, or share a password or one-time code are high-risk. Poor spelling can be a clue, but polished writing does not prove a message is real. A cue is evidence to slow down, not a complete identity test. Do not click, reply, transfer, or share secrets while pressured.
Slide 3: Verify through a separate route
Do not use the contact path supplied by the suspicious message. PAUSE; Find the official service independently; Ask if the request is real; Act only through a verified route. Known app • saved statement • official website typed independently
For a bank concern, open the known app or use contact details from a bank card or statement. Do not call a number included only in the unexpected text, and do not trust caller ID by itself. For a web notice, navigate to the known official site yourself rather than following a message link. If uncertain, talk to a trusted adult and ask the institution through an independently found route. A search result or advertisement may also be misleading; use the known official domain.
Slide 4: CRA contact needs a precise rule
CRA may contact people; caller ID is not proof. CRA may call, write, or send notifications; Caller ID can be spoofed; Never share passwords or security codes; Ask, end, verify independently if unsure. Use the CRA contact-verification tool or Canada.ca details.
Do not memorize the false rule “CRA never calls.” The Canada Revenue Agency may contact people by phone and other channels. A caller ID that displays a government name still does not prove who is calling. If a person is unsure, they can ask for the caller’s name, office, and callback number, end the call, and check using CRA’s official contact-verification tool or contact details found independently on Canada.ca. CRA may request some information for a legitimate identity check or missing tax information, but never share passwords or one-time security codes with an unexpected caller.
Slide 5: Pause: classify before you respond
Name the action, cue, and independent check. Message A: requested action?; Message B: safe route?; What remains uncertain?. Pause and write one sentence for each contact.
For the two fictional contacts, identify the requested action, one warning cue, and the verification route. Pause before choosing.
Slide 6: Worked answer: safe without guessing
Verify the contact; do not make an irreversible move. A  Do not transfer or share the code; contact the bank independently.; B  Navigate to Canada.ca yourself and check for the notice.; Unknown sender identity? Verify before acting.. Appearance is a clue—not authentication.
For message A, the safe-account transfer and code request are high-risk. Do not transfer or reply; contact the bank independently. For message B, the notification may be legitimate, but this fictional card is not proof. Navigate to Canada.ca yourself and check the account through the official route. If a caller claims to be CRA, remember that CRA can call, but caller ID can be spoofed. Ask for callback details, end the call, and verify independently if unsure. The lesson is neither “trust it” nor “all contacts are fake.” It is pause, verify, then act. If a learner already clicked or shared information, the response changes: stop interacting, secure the affected account from a trusted device, and promptly contact the relevant institution through an independently found route. Preserve the message and time, but do not reopen its link to collect evidence. If money was lost, contact local police promptly and report through current Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre guidance. Reporting does not guarantee recovery. A second person offering guaranteed reimbursement for an upfront fee is another reason to pause and verify.
Original CALM 10 classroom demonstration. Figures and people in this example are fictional; check current sources before real decisions.
Follow a complete example
For A, I ignore the polished appearance and read the request. Moving a balance to a stranger's “protected account” and sending a sign-in code could give away funds and access. The warning cues justify refusing those actions now. I can do that without first proving the sender's identity.
Connect the video to this task. Apply FINLIT’s pause-and-check advice separately to both contacts. A dangerous instruction and a potentially genuine call still require different explanations and independent checks.


For B, the request is different. CRA can seek supporting information, and the caller offers details for checking. That is compatible with a genuine call, but it remains an unverified claim. I use the official process before discussing personal tax information.


Complete response record:




A resembles bank-investigator impersonation: it requests a balance transfer and a sign-in code under time pressure and secrecy. Leah should not transfer, share the code, reply through the text or install anything. Open the known bank app or use the number on the existing bank card to ask whether the bank has a real concern. The source record supports that separate route; a logo does not authenticate this sender.


B may be genuine because CRA can call about tax documents. Leah should request the claimed name, office and callback details, say the contact will be checked, and end the call without sharing personal information. Reach CRA's verification page independently and use its official checking/contact route. If the number is not in the tool, obtain further official verification because direct employee numbers may be absent. Only continue the real matter through a verified channel; do not assume a caller-ID label or a polite tone proves authenticity.




“Block all government contact forever” would leave possible real business unresolved. “Send the code to show cooperation” would hand the unverified sender a sensitive tool. The plan protects access while keeping a route for legitimate service.

Devon's job offer and appointment call

The unrequested work message matches job-fraud warning patterns: it demands a deposit to unlock work and asks Devon to receive and forward money through a personal account. It also discourages independent contact. A real company can be impersonated. Devon should not deposit, forward funds, install a dashboard or provide documents. Independently find the actual employer's official contact and ask whether this vacancy and recruiter/program are authorized; do not use only the message's chat. If not verifiable, do not proceed with the risky requests.


The appointment call could be genuine because Devon made an appointment request, and this exchange asks for no sensitive action. The sender is still unverified. Devon can end the call, open the previously installed bank app directly to review the original request, or use the number on the bank card to confirm the appointment. Handle a confirmed appointment through that verified channel. If the institution rejects the request, preserve/report the suspicious approach; if it remains unresolved, do not reveal secrets or pay to resolve the uncertainty. The September 28 source record supports independent verification rather than judging a contact by appearance or treating every call as fake.

Core vocabulary
Information or access has been revealed to someone who should not have it.
Information or access has actually been used improperly.
An active signed-in connection that may remain open under a service's rules.
The genuine provider's process for regaining or protecting account access.
Start here
If someone has entered information into a suspicious page, shame and panic can delay useful action. A response starts with a more practical question: what information or access was actually exposed? An account password, payment card and downloaded remote-control app create different response needs.


You will work through a password-exposure log, construct a follow-up using a supplied provider guide, and then write a new response for exposed card details and an unrecognized transaction. The final product is a prioritized action plan that states each recipient's role and preserves evidence without exposing secrets again.


Use Meet the situation and read the documents → Learn the method → Follow a complete example → Practise with support → Check your understanding → Apply independently → Review and complete. Pause after the worked response if helpful. All actions are written plans; do not change a real account or call a provider. Guided activities and six questions are practice. The independent response plan and sign-offs complete the lesson. Your work saves automatically.


Vocabulary. Exposure means information or access may have become available to someone who should not have it. Compromise means security has been breached; an exposure can justify protective action before every outcome is known. A session is a continuing signed-in connection. Revoking a session ends that connection using the service's controls. A trusted device is one the person has reason to rely on, rather than one possibly under an unexpected caller's control. An unauthorized transaction is generally a transaction the person did not make or approve; provider agreements and investigation matter.


Optional disclosure: Official response guidance. Dated in-course records contain the required information. Live pages support current real use but are not required lesson stops.


Meet the situation and read the documents


Finley is a fictional adult with a music-service account and a separate email account. At 3:20 p.m. on October 8, 2026, Finley entered a music-service password on a page reached from an unexpected message. Finley then noticed the page was a look-alike and stopped. The actual password and page address are omitted.


Document A — Exposure log






Question
Supplied answer





What was entered?
Music-account login name and password only.




Was that password reused?
Yes, on Finley's email account. The email is also the music account's recovery address.




Money/card/identity details?
No payment, card details, Social Insurance Number (SIN), identity document or tax information was entered. No money loss is known.




Software or device access?
No download, app installation or remote-access permission occurred. This does not certify the device's condition; it records what Finley did.




What is available?
Finley's own updated phone, not used for the suspicious page, with the known email app and a saved official music-service bookmark.




Access status
Finley can still access both services through those known routes. No recovery change is known.




Evidence already available
Original message, time 3:20 p.m., and a screenshot without the password. No need to reopen the suspicious page.





Document B — Fictional provider security guide


Both fictional services provide these controls through their genuine settings. This is a supplied case guide, not a claim about every real service's interface.


    

  1. Change the password to a different strong credential for this service.
    2. 

  2. Review recovery email/phone entries and ask official support about unrecognized changes.
    3. 

  3. Review signed-in sessions. Changing the password does not automatically end all existing sessions on these particular services. Use Sign out other sessions to end them.
    4. 

  4. Turn on supported MFA, following the service's recovery guidance.
    5. 

  5. If access is lost or a change cannot be corrected, use official account-recovery support reached from the known service, not the suspicious message.
    6. 



Document C — In-course response and rights records


Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, “Protecting yourself from identity theft online,” “Protecting your digital identity” and “Addressing digital identity theft”; checked September 28, 2026. Identify affected information and contact affected account providers. Change compromised/reused credentials and consider connected recovery accounts. Keep software current and monitor activity. Broader identity-fraud measures depend on what identity information or misuse is involved; do not invent exposed data.


Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC), “Resolving an unauthorized transaction” and “Unauthorized credit and debit transactions: know your rights and responsibilities”; checked September 28, 2026. If card/account misuse is suspected or at risk, notify the institution or card issuer without delay and follow its security/dispute process. Federally regulated institutions must investigate disputed unauthorized transactions; use of an authentication method alone does not establish the customer's responsibility. Agreements, circumstances and prompt reporting matter. The course cannot promise a refund or decide liability.


CAFC, “What to do if you're a victim of fraud”; checked September 28, 2026. Keep relevant documents and messages, contact the institution that transferred money when money is involved, report fraud to local police and through the official fraud/cybercrime reporting route. Reports support a response and investigation; they do not reset an account or guarantee recovery. Immediate danger needs emergency help, not waiting for a report review.


Read the documents


What is the confirmed exposure in Finley's record? Choose and select Check document reading.
Learn the method
Contain the exposure without waiting for certainty


Stop interacting with the suspicious page or caller. Do not send another code, pay to cancel a request or keep testing the page. Protective action can be appropriate even before the person knows whether the information has been used. Finley's password entry justifies securing the affected accounts; it does not justify inventing a stolen SIN.


An action plan should name both the risk and the control. “Fix the phone” is vague. “Use the separate updated phone to open the known email app and secure its recovery settings” tells the reader which route is being used and why. If a device may be under remote control or contain installed malicious software, stop using it for sensitive sign-ins and obtain official device/security support from a different trusted device. Removing an icon is not proof that access is gone. No such installation is reported in Finley's case.


Follow the account connections


Finley's email can reset the music account. If both use the same exposed password, changing only the music password leaves an important route at risk. A defensible sequence is to secure the recovery email first, promptly secure the music account next, and then review sessions, recovery entries and MFA on both. If access were already lost, official recovery support might have to come earlier.


The sequence is based on the supplied relationship, not a universal rule that email always comes before a bank emergency. If money is actively being moved, prompt financial-institution contact may be the most urgent action. Explain your priority with the case facts.


Check whether a change actually closes access


Password changes, session controls and MFA do related but different jobs. In these fictional services, an already signed-in session can remain after a password change. The guide therefore requires reviewing and ending other sessions separately. MFA helps protect future sign-ins; it does not undo information already taken.


The record is not complete when it says “changed something.” Log what was done, when and through which independently reached service. Then note what remains unresolved. If a recovery address is unfamiliar or access is blocked, official provider support has information and controls a classroom model cannot supply.


Separate account security from a transaction dispute






Exposure or observation
Recipient/control that fits
What that action cannot do alone





Entered/reused password
Affected account providers; change credentials, review recovery/session controls.
Determine or reverse a card charge.




Exposed card details or unrecognized charge
Card issuer/financial institution, reached independently; secure card and investigate disputed activity.
Secure an unrelated email password.




Unwanted installed access
Official device/security support and affected providers from a trusted route.
Guarantee the device is clean merely because an app icon disappeared.




Identity fraud or money loss
Relevant providers, police and official fraud-reporting route.
Guarantee reimbursement or replace urgent provider contact.





A merchant disagreement is also different from a transaction the person did not make or approve. For example, a person may recognize a purchase but dispute its description or cancellation. The next lesson examines that evidence. Describe the facts truthfully to the issuer rather than labelling every unwanted charge “unauthorized.”


Preserve useful evidence without preserving secrets


A log should include the date/time, contact or merchant label, requested action, amount if any, what was disclosed by category, actions taken and reference numbers. It should not contain the actual password, one-time code, full card number or SIN. Keep a safe original message or screenshot already available; do not reopen a dangerous link to improve a report. Share sensitive originals only through the institution's independently verified secure process if needed in real life, not through coursework or public posts.


Optional first-step hint: “Start the guided response with two account names and the arrow 'email recovery → music account.' That connection explains the priority.”


Follow a complete example
I first record what was exposed and what was not. Finley's music password was entered, and it is also the email password. The record says no card, SIN or tax data was entered. I keep those limits visible so the response fits the event.


The recovery relationship tells me why the email needs prompt attention. I use the separate updated phone and independently known app/bookmark. I also read the provider guide carefully: password changes do not end existing sessions in this exercise, so I cannot stop after the change.


Complete response plan:




October 8, 2026, 3:20 p.m.: Finley entered the music login and password on a look-alike page. The same password is used for the recovery email account. No payment/card, SIN, tax data or remote-access installation is known. Stop using the suspicious page and do not provide any further information. From the separate updated phone, open the known email app and promptly secure that recovery account with a unique strong credential, recovery review and the supplied session/MFA controls. Then use the saved official music bookmark to replace its password with a different strong credential and apply the same checks. Sign out other sessions on both because their guide says a password change alone does not end them.


Preserve the original message, password-free screenshot and event time; record the security actions without recording credentials. If access changes, recovery entries are unfamiliar or controls cannot be completed, use the affected provider's official recovery support. Monitor both services. The Canadian source record supports addressing affected and connected accounts. No known financial transfer exists here, so do not write that a bank has reversed money or that a police case has already been opened. The suspected phishing can be reported through the official fraud/cybercrime route, alongside rather than instead of account security.




“Only change the music password” misses the recovery path. “Buy a guaranteed cleanup from the message sender” hands control back to the same unverified source.


Next: Practise with support. Try “What has been completed, and what remains uncertain?” before opening its comparison model.

Both services' MFA setup remains unfinished.

Apply independently
René's card exposure


René is a fictional adult. Create a card-response and evidence plan from these new documents. This case does not expose an account password.


Document D — Incident log, October 10, 2026. At 1:05 p.m., René entered a name, mailing address and credit-card details into an unexpected parcel-fee page. No bank/app password, PIN, one-time code, SIN or identity document was entered. No app was downloaded or remote access granted. The card details themselves are not shown. René stopped when the page demanded an extra code and did not provide one. A separate updated device with the previously installed genuine card-issuer app is available.


Document E — Independently reached account record. At 1:20 p.m., René opened the genuine issuer app directly. It showed an $84.00 transaction labelled “Harbour Electronics.” René did not make or approve that transaction and has no purchase from that merchant. The physical card is still held. The issuer is a federally regulated Canadian bank. Its supplied help instructions say to contact card security promptly for exposed details or transactions not approved; the current official number is available on the card and in the genuine app. No report, block or reimbursement has occurred yet.


Document F — Evidence available. The original parcel message and a screenshot with no full card number or code are saved. The transaction time/merchant label are visible in the genuine app. There is no evidence of a new credit account or change to a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) account. A stranger has offered to “cancel the charge” if René sends the missing code; that stranger is not verified.


Use four fields:


    

  • Exposure and evidence boundaries — name what was entered, the independently observed transaction and what is not established. Distinguish card data from a stolen bank password.
    • 

  • Prioritized immediate response — give three or four actions, including the correct first financial recipient and a safe route, and explain the priority.
    • 

  • Privacy-safe evidence entry — write a dated entry including amount, merchant label, categories disclosed and pending actions, without actual account data.
    • 

  • Follow-up, rights and limits — explain issuer investigation/monitoring, appropriate fraud reporting, and why neither a stranger's offer nor a classroom answer guarantees recovery.
    •

René disclosed name, address and card details, then saw an $84.00 Harbour Electronics transaction in the independently opened issuer app that René did not make or approve. No banking password, PIN, code, SIN, installed access or CRA change is supplied. Stop interacting with the parcel page and do not give the stranger a code. Promptly contact the bank's card-security team through the existing card or genuine app using the separate updated device. Explain the exposed details and disputed transaction; follow the issuer's blocking/replacement, account-security and dispute instructions. Preserve already available evidence without delaying urgent issuer contact.


October 10, 2026: card details, name and mailing address entered at 1:05 p.m.; no additional code provided. At 1:20 p.m., genuine app showed $84.00 Harbour Electronics transaction not made or approved by René. Message and password/card-free screenshot retained. Issuer contact, protection instructions and dispute reference are pending; no refund is recorded. Record later actions and references as they occur.


The federally regulated issuer must investigate the disputed unauthorized transaction and can advise on the card/payment route. René should monitor the account, cooperate with the process and keep the issuer's replies. Fraud can also be reported to local police and the official CAFC-linked reporting route; that does not itself block the card or guarantee reimbursement. Do not send the stranger money or a code. No new credit account or tax misuse is established, so do not invent those outcomes or claim every agency has already acted.

Lessons
Bring your decisions together


A portfolio is a small, explained selection of work. Choose evidence that shows a decision, its reasons and an improvement. You do not need a paid job or personal financial records. Use your own learning actions in this course; money and workplace examples can remain fictional.


Work on the four parts below across the final weeks. For each part, choose the relevant lesson from a dropdown, review your saved answer and write the requested explanation. The course shows the selected answer read-only beside the portfolio fields. Missing lesson work has a link to the lesson; it is never filled by a model without your action.


Part 1 — A strength, a goal and the next step


Choose one actual action you took while learning here: checked a calculation, compared two dated claims, revised a sentence to remove an exaggeration, or corrected a plan after feedback. Explain what that action suggests about a skill and what it does not yet prove.


Read a portfolio example
Complete example: “In Read a pay stub, I checked the current deductions instead of using the year-to-date column, then revised my calculation. This suggests careful checking after feedback; one corrected example does not establish payroll expertise. I would like to explore work that uses organized records, while keeping time for activities outside school. My next step is to check both dates and totals in Build a flexible budget, then review the first attempt against the model. The route records in Build a high-school route with checkpoints show how prerequisites link together; I still need to verify which actual courses prepare for a real records-related program before using that as my own school plan.”


Specific checks: own observable course action; cautious skill claim; direction and life priority; feasible next step and clearly labelled unverified question.


Part 2 — A money decision with a revision


Select one of the five final tasks below. Explain its original constraint and one calculation, then use the listed change. Every other fact in that independent case remains the same. These are separate hypothetical versions; do not move facts from the lesson's guided case into its independent case.






Final task
Exact changed condition





Compare a major purchase: Riley
Total cash available for the tool choice is $130 instead of $140.




What a major purchase really costs: Lee
Total seasonal budget is $540 instead of $550.




Give a savings goal a job: Lena
A one-time $10 required cost is deducted from the eighth weekly contribution before the fee is paid. The first seven contributions remain $18 each; only $8 of the eighth is available for this fee.




Choose what the next dollar does: Jules
The extra amount available before the repair deadline is $30 instead of $40. The saved $60 remains.




Check what your money will buy: Riley
Current savings are $238 instead of $248. The confirmed later $10 and the case's prices/dates remain.





Do not invent an interest rate, approval, price reduction or extra income. A sound revision can identify an unresolved gap and the exact option that would need confirmation.


Read a portfolio example
Example using Give a savings goal a job: “Lena has $18 weekly for an eight-week $144 fee, so 8 × $18 meets it exactly. I would pause the $6 hobby contribution because no additional money is supplied. With the new $10 cost taken from the eighth contribution, the fee fund would reach 7 × $18 + $8 = $134 and be $10 short. I could identify that gap and investigate a confirmed extension or lower-cost alternative; I could not claim either exists. The original plan depends on all eight contributions being available.”


Checks: correct base facts and units; visible calculation; change affects the conclusion; no invented resource.


Part 3 — A safe response and its limit


Select a workplace or personal-information lesson. Explain the action you chose, the evidence for it, the appropriate person/organization and one limit to what the record establishes.


Read a portfolio example
Example: “In the library shift, the spill blocks the shorter route and the cleaning spray requires training. Rowan should keep clear, place the cone only if it can be reached safely and contact Morgan using the supplied extension. The activity-room route is clear on the floor plan. Rowan should not use the spray or change a record without authority. This is a decision within the supplied exercise; it does not prove workplace training or supervised experience.”


Checks: hazard/exposure identified; action fits supplied authority; correct contact/route; uncertainty or limit stated.


Part 4 — Show the improvement


Select one answer you revised. Display the earlier saved version if available, or let the learner quote a short earlier sentence from their own notes. A missing earlier version is not fabricated; they may describe the specific weakness and quote the current sentence instead.


Read a portfolio example
Example: “My earlier interview sentence called Rowan an expert at records. The supplied open-house record showed that Rowan noticed activity cards under the wrong headings, checked the approved list with the lead and relabelled the stacks with confirmation. I changed it to describe those actions and the result: visitors received the intended card. The revised claim is narrower and supported. In my next application example, I will check that every result comes from the supplied record.”

Career planning and future readiness · Lesson 6
Explore employment and entrepreneurship routes
How to complete this lesson
  1. Start here
  2. Meet the situation and read the documents
  3. Learn the method
  4. Watch or read The Entrepreneur’s Dozen; try the short case check
  5. Follow a complete example
  6. Practise with support
  7. Check your understanding
  8. Apply independently
  9. Review and complete
At a check, try an answer, read the hint and revise. A different incorrect answer brings method support and an option to show the worked reasoning. Written responses use the comparison and self-checks; they are not automatically graded.
Optional reference · Choose the Way You Work — alis
All facts needed for the activities are supplied in the lesson. Use the named original for further reading or to check current details.
Open Choose the Way You Work — alis ↗
Core vocabulary
Work performed for an employer under the arrangement's stated terms.
Organizing a venture that provides a product or service and carries its own costs and risks.
Money received by a venture before subtracting its expenses.
Revenue left after the included expenses are subtracted; it is not the same as revenue.
Start here
Enjoying a task does not settle how to earn from it


Kai enjoys working with bicycles. A shop offers a fictional paid helper shift, and a small service idea also looks interesting. Both connect with the same interest, but they involve different responsibilities, support and uncertainty.


You will compare employment with a small venture, calculate money remaining after listed costs and revise a plan after customer information changes. Your final product compares two routes for Samir, a different fictional learner. All sales, work and feedback are supplied scenarios. You will not sell anything, contact customers, apply for work or repair equipment to complete this lesson.


Follow Meet the situation, Learn the method, Follow a complete example, Practise with support, Check your understanding, Apply independently and Review and complete. Pause after the calculations if useful. Practice is saved but is not final evidence. Samir's comparison is the final saved product; its completion is your sign-off rather than an automated judgement of a business idea.


Meet the situation and read the documents


Kai's starting evidence


Kai is a fictional 19-year-old who has completed Grade 12. During eight community workshop sessions, Kai checked part labels against an inventory list, explained completed steps to visitors and asked the workshop leader before unfamiliar work. Kai has not had a paid repair-shop job. Kai likes practical work and explaining it, wants to develop technical knowledge and values a predictable short weekly shift.


A work offer record describes what a particular employer is offering. A venture record organizes a person's proposed sales and expenses. The documents below are original fiction, with invented prices and wages; they are not current offers or legal guidance.


Cedar Cycle shop helper offer


One four-hour Saturday helper shift at $18 per hour, before payroll deductions. The shop schedules customers, supplies tools and materials, handles payments and directs the work. Kai would check inventory, explain the service-booking process and ask the supervisor about unfamiliar requests. Training for those duties is provided. Kai is not being hired as an independent repair technician. This record confirms one offered shift only; later hours are unknown.


Kai's first-week service trial


For the scenario, five service jobs are completed under appropriate workshop supervision and all five customers pay $30. Replacement parts cost $75 in total; transport and other supplies cost $25 in total. Kai spends six hours on the work and administration. The record does not price equipment wear, insurance, permits, taxes or payment for Kai's time. It supplies no evidence of next week's demand. The activity is a paper case, not permission to operate a real service.


Kai's initial claim


“Five customers paid $30, so I made $150 profit. If I like repairs, running my own business must be the best route.”


Reading check: Which responsibility belongs to the shop in the Cedar Cycle offer?
Learn the method
Compare the way of working as well as the task


An employee works within an employer's direction and arrangements. A self-employed person is responsible for obtaining work from clients rather than being on an employer's payroll. Entrepreneurship involves developing an opportunity and taking on the uncertainty of offering a product or service. A venture can be small; size alone does not remove its responsibilities.


The same interest can appear in either route. Kai may enjoy bicycles while preferring the shop's scheduling and supervision. Or Kai may want to learn about pricing and customer needs as well as technical work. Neither preference makes a person more capable or more ambitious. The useful question is which responsibilities and supports fit the current goal.


Dated reference record: Alberta’s career site alis, in Choose the Way You Work, read September 28, 2026, distinguishes employee arrangements from self-employment and discusses finding clients, unpaid business-development time and learning business skills. This lesson's two records provide the details to compare. Optional: open Choose the Way You Work — alis (new tab) ↗.


Follow the money through the record


Revenue is money from sales before expenses. An expense is a cost of providing the product or service. Subtracting the listed expenses gives an amount remaining under the supplied assumptions. If some costs are not recorded, do not label that remainder complete profit or take-home pay.


Use the flow number of paid sales × price → revenue → subtract listed costs → remainder before unlisted costs/time. It keeps a sales headline from hiding the resources used to earn it. A fixed cost stays the same in the particular scenario; a per-item cost repeats for every item. Fewer sales do not necessarily reduce every expense.


Wages before payroll deductions are also different from take-home pay. Four hours at $18 produces a gross wage calculation, not proof of the amount deposited. Comparing that wage directly with a venture's incomplete remainder as if both were final income would mislead. Explain the categories and missing information before making a recommendation.


Test an opportunity without pretending demand is certain


A person liking an idea is not the same as paying the proposed price. One week's sales do not establish reliable future demand. Consider who needs the service, what alternatives they have and what conditions they will accept. Customer feedback can justify changing the size, timing or scope of an offer. It does not justify removing a necessary safety step or pretending a material cost has disappeared.


For this course, testing means using supplied scenario cards and calculations. A next learning step can be making a more complete cost record or revising an explanation. No real purchase, customer research or unsupervised work is required.


Prepare truthful evidence for an employment route


A résumé summarizes relevant skills, education and experience in an organized record. A basic structure is a name/contact heading, a short relevant summary, skills supported by examples, dated experience entries and education/training. Real applications may need contact information; a public practice page should not display private addresses, identification numbers or other people's information.


Using only the Cedar Cycle offer and Kai's starting evidence, this compact fictional résumé section would be truthful:


Kai — practice candidate; private contact details omitted


Summary: Interested in supervised bicycle-shop helper work and developing technical knowledge.


Relevant experience: Community workshop participant, eight sessions. Checked part labels against an inventory list; explained completed steps to visitors; asked the leader before unfamiliar work.


Education: Grade 12 completed in this fictional case.


This describes experience without changing it into a paid job. A cover letter is a message to a particular employer explaining why selected evidence fits the opening. For the Cedar Cycle offer, a truthful sentence would be: “My workshop experience checking labels against a list relates to your inventory duty.” A portfolio contains selected examples with explanations, rather than every file a person owns. An online employment profile presents relevant background on a digital service; it is not a reason to post private documents publicly. No résumé, message or profile is sent in this lesson.


For example, a portfolio could contain a blank sample inventory checklist that Kai created to demonstrate the checking method, accompanied by a note explaining the task and Kai's contribution. A visitor's identifiable repair form would be a poor public sample: it could reveal someone else's details and would not by itself explain Kai's work. Select the minimum relevant evidence and remove private information. A cover letter then points the employer to the useful example; it does not need to retell every item in the résumé.


Show a first-step hint
Optional hint: Before subtracting, label each amount “sales,” “listed cost,” “gross wage” or “not supplied.” That label often reveals a misleading comparison.


Watch or read · FINLIT 101
The Entrepreneur’s Dozen
Kai’s records describe one employment offer and one small venture trial. Watch or read the advice about researching an opportunity, anticipating problems and revising an idea. Look for reasons to test a venture rather than assume enthusiasm is enough.
Read the video transcript
Visuals: simple drawings place opportunity at a target and balance risk with reward. The drawings are concepts, not a measure of how likely a business is to succeed.
in entrepreneurial activity. An entrepreneur examines needs, wants, and problems, and then tries to think about if a better solution can be created. Narrows the possible opportunities down to one specific opportunity. Thinks of an innovative idea to address the identified opportunity, researches the opportunity and idea thoroughly, enlists the best experts, sources of advice and assistance that can be found, plans the venture and looks for possible problems that might arise, weighs the risks and possible rewards, and then makes a decision. Never gets tied to a specific idea, even if they personally love it, if research shows it's not likely to work. Employs the resources necessary for the venture if the decision is made to go ahead. Understands that any entrepreneurial venture will take a great deal of long, hard work. Realizes a sense of accomplishment from successful ventures and learns lessons for the future. One of the biggest things that leads to success as an entrepreneur is ensuring you've identified
FINLIT 101 · The Entrepreneur’s Dozen · selected excerpt, used with permission.
What still needs investigation before Kai treats the five-sale trial as a dependable income?
This short practice check saves with your lesson work. You can change your answer after reading the feedback.
Follow a complete example
Correct Kai's claim and compare the routes
Connect the video to this task. As the example separates sales from money remaining, connect it to FINLIT’s advice to test resources and risks. Missing costs remain missing after the arithmetic.


The claim starts with a valid multiplication: five paid jobs × $30 = $150 revenue. The error is naming that entire amount profit. The record lists $75 parts and $25 other costs. Subtracting both leaves $50. Time and other potential costs have not been valued, so I keep that boundary in the sentence.


The shop offer provides a different calculation: four hours × $18 = $72 gross wages for the one offered shift. That is not a complete after-deduction amount. It also comes with different responsibilities: the shop handles booking, equipment and customer payments, while Kai works under its direction.


Completed comparison: “Kai's first-week trial records $150 revenue, $100 listed costs and $50 remaining before unlisted costs or payment for Kai's six hours. It does not prove $150 profit or recurring weekly sales. The Cedar Cycle offer provides $72 gross wages for one supervised four-hour shift, with the shop handling customers, tools and payments. I would investigate the shop helper route first because Kai wants technical learning and a predictable short shift. The service idea could remain a learning project for understanding costs and customer needs. Before treating it as an earning plan, its missing costs and repeat demand would need evidence.”


“Employment means no responsibility” would also be wrong. Kai still needs accuracy, truthful communication and appropriate requests for help. The distinction is which responsibilities each record assigns, not whether one route requires effort.

Balance a plan when life changes

Core vocabulary
The time and resources actually available after existing commitments.
Time or money left available for variation or unexpected needs.
Something given preference when resources cannot cover every option.
A specific change to a plan in response to evidence or a changed condition.
Start here
Keep the goal visible while changing the route


Maya has planned two hours a week to explore design work. A new family commitment makes one trip impossible. Removing rest or pretending travel takes no time would make the timetable look tidy without making it workable.


You will revise Maya's plan using supplied schedules and an alternatives notice. Your final product revises a different plan for Arun. These are fictional people with complete planning records; you do not need to disclose your family circumstances or arrange a real visit. All required work is completed on this page.


Follow Meet the situation, Learn the method, Follow a complete example, Practise with support, Check your understanding, Apply independently and Review and complete. Take the break you need between the two planning cases. Read the clocks carefully and save a little time for checking the sequence. Practice and the final revision save separately.


Meet the situation and read the documents


Maya's purpose and current week


Maya wants to create two sample layouts over four weeks to learn whether design tasks remain interesting beyond a first attempt. The plan reserves two one-hour exploration sessions each week. Maya also values keeping existing family commitments and a protected Saturday rest period. This is a learning goal, not an admission requirement or promise of a design career.


A weekly planning board shows how commitments share limited time. A fixed commitment cannot be moved within this case; a flexible block may be reassigned. The labels describe the supplied situation, not a rule about every person's schedule.

Maya now has a fixed family commitment at home on Tuesdays from 15:30 to 17:30 for four weeks. Thursday's original travel remains available. Maya wants to keep the design-learning goal if a supplied option fits.


The design club's alternative activity notice


“The Tuesday introduction is also available as a self-guided written package. Allow 40 minutes to follow the example and 20 minutes to draft a layout. It covers the same introductory task and can be used in any available one-hour block at home. No call, meeting or account setup is needed in this scenario. Thursday's practice remains a one-hour session. Maya has the device and materials for the written package. There is no fee.”


Reading check: Why does the original Tuesday route no longer work? Select 
Learn the method
Separate goal, route and timing


A goal is what you are trying to accomplish. A route is the way you will work toward it. Timing places the route into an actual day or week. Maya's goal is to explore design through two samples. The club and written package are possible routes. Tuesday or Saturday are possible times if they fit the records.


A changed constraint does not automatically cancel the goal. It does require checking the route. Conversely, new experience might show that the goal itself no longer fits. The useful question is which part the new evidence changes, rather than treating every revision as failure.


Count the whole block


An hour-long session can require two hours when travel is included. Do not overlap travel with the task that requires being somewhere else. A plan must also allow transitions: putting materials away, getting ready for the next commitment or dealing with a small delay. A buffer is time left unassigned so every step does not depend on a perfect sequence.


Use the time line:


Travel or preparation → focused activity → return or transition → next commitment.


If any part overlaps a fixed commitment, the route needs a change. Having a total number of “free hours” is not enough if those hours occur at the wrong time or in fragments too short for the task.


Make digital habits serve the plan


Digital tools can support planning through calendars, reminders, saved notes and accessible materials. They can also consume the time reserved for the task. In a one-hour block, repeated message checking can leave less time for the example and draft even though the calendar still says “one hour.” A useful plan names one manageable habit: silence nonessential notifications during the example, keep the task document visible or put a reminder at the transition time.


The habit is a support, not a claim that everyone can solve every barrier through willpower. If the required task still cannot fit, revise the route or amount of work. Keep privacy in mind when using a digital planner: fictional labels are enough for this course, and a public calendar need not reveal another person's personal circumstances.


Treat overload as information


Time pressure can make a plan stressful. A reasonable planning response is to reduce conflicting demands, break a task into workable pieces or use an available support. Removing sleep, meals or all recovery to make the chart balance would hide a new problem. In this case the protected rest period stays protected.


Support does not have to mean someone making the decision for you. Here the alternative written package and clear scheduling notice provide support. A precise future question can identify an uncertainty; no actual message needs to be sent to finish the lesson.


State when the plan will be reviewed


A revision note should record old assumption → new evidence → changed route/timing → review trigger. A review trigger is the event that makes another look useful: a changed timetable, unavailable materials or evidence that the task takes longer than planned. Include a date too, so “review later” becomes an action you can locate.


Dated reference record: Alberta’s career site alis, in Why Career Planning Can Work for You, read September 28, 2026, describes career planning as continuing work shaped by changing priorities and realities, with goals broken into ordered steps. In this lesson, the schedules make those changes concrete. Optional: open Why Career Planning Can Work for You — alis (new tab) ↗.


Show a first-step hint
Optional hint: Mark the fixed conflict first. Then look for an explicitly supplied alternative that fits one of the listed flexible blocks.


Follow a complete example
Replace Maya's Tuesday route


I begin with the old assumption: Maya could leave home at 15:30 on Tuesday and return at 17:30. The new family commitment uses that entire interval. Moving only the session label would not solve the travel conflict.


The club's alternative activity notice supplies a written alternative taking 40 + 20 = 60 minutes. Maya's original weekly plan supplies a full hour at home on Saturday from 10:00 to 11:00, with the device/materials available. This is a supported replacement; I am not inventing an online class or permission. Thursday's existing session remains feasible under the new commitments notice.


Revised board: Tuesday 15:30–17:30 stays with the family commitment. Thursday keeps the 15:30 departure, 16:00–17:00 practice and 17:30 return. Saturday 10:00–10:40 becomes the written example and 10:40–11:00 the layout draft. Saturday 11:00–11:30 remains a buffer, and 14:00–16:00 remains rest/recreation.


Completed revision note: “The old plan assumed Tuesday travel was available. The new four-week family commitment removes that route, but the design-learning goal still matters to Maya. The supplied one-hour written package fits Saturday 10:00–11:00 without changing Thursday or the protected rest block. During the example, Maya can silence nonessential notifications and use an 11:00 reminder to stop and review. On Sunday October 11, review whether the written work actually fitted the hour. If it took longer, revise the next week's task size or use another supplied option rather than consuming the protected rest time.”


The unsupported alternative “do both the family commitment and travel” makes two simultaneous demands. “An online session must be available Wednesday” invents an option. The revised board works because its timing and alternative both appear in the documents.

Thursday 16:00–17:00 at home is free; no travel is required for this alternative.

Use Check my revision. The second choice uses the new notice. The first retains an impossible step. The third disregards the protected block even though a workable option is supplied.
